01

The delivery

On 22 October 2024 an Associated Press photographer stood in Ghobeiri, in Beirut's southern suburbs, and photographed a 2,000-lb warhead in the eight seconds before it reached an apartment block. Arms researchers identified the guidance kit strapped to it as a Rafael SPICE — the same kit family sold under the $320 million commercial licence recorded in row three of the ledger below.

01 / 06
Ghobeiri, Beirut · 22 Oct 2024 · Bilal Hussein / AP
02

What this record is

A congressional notification is an approval to sell — not a delivery. The distinction is the single most abused fact in reporting on this subject, and it is the organising principle of everything below. A $20 billion headline can contain no bombs at all; a $2 billion line can contain thirty-five thousand of them.

FMF

Foreign Military Financing

U.S. grant aid. Israel receives $3.8 billion a year under the 2016–2028 memorandum of understanding, which it then spends on American defence articles.

FMS

Foreign Military Sales

Government-to-government sale brokered by the Defense Security Cooperation Agency. Above set thresholds it triggers a 36(b) notification and a 15-day congressional review window.

DCS

Direct Commercial Sale

A contract directly between a U.S. manufacturer and Israel, licensed by the State Department. Far less publicly visible than FMS — and the least documented channel in this file.

WRSA-I

War Reserve Stockpile

U.S.-owned munitions pre-positioned on Israeli soil, which Israel may be authorised to draw from. Drawn down heavily in the opening months of the Gaza war.

§36(b)

Emergency Waiver

The Secretary of State may declare that "an emergency exists" and waive the review period outright. Used for Israel twice in December 2023, three times in February 2025, and twice in 2026.

04

Six frames

Three weeks after Ghobeiri, on 15 November 2024, Associated Press photographer Hassan Ammar trained a long lens on an eleven-storey apartment block in Tayouneh and waited. The Israeli military had issued an evacuation warning with a map marking the building. Read left to right: the munition in flight, detonation at the lower floors, collapse. Every line in the ledger above resolves, eventually, into one of these.

05

One dot is one thousand warheads

Every 2,000-lb class warhead in the record since October 2023, sorted into the only three states that matter: gone, bought, or merely floated. The gap between the filled and the hollow dots is the whole argument about what these numbers mean.

≈16,800 transferred. Physically delivered and overwhelmingly expended — the ≥14,000 MK-84s and ~1,000 penetrators reported by U.S. officials in June 2024, plus the 1,800 released from hold in 2025.
39,529 approved. Notified, contracted, largely unbuilt. The February 2025 emergency cases: 35,529 general-purpose bodies and 4,000 I-2000 penetrators, deliveries stated to begin 2026.
60,000 proposed. The September 2026 package — 40,000 GP bodies and 20,000 penetrators — still at informal notification. Nothing has been signed, built or shipped.

The comparison that cuts the other way

Tonnage comparisons flatter whichever side is making them, so here is the one that does not help this page's framing. Between 1964 and 1973 the United States dropped roughly 7,662,000 tons of ordnance on Indochina, and 2,150,000 tons across all theatres of the Second World War. Against Vietnam, the entire record on this page — every bomb delivered, approved and proposed since October 2023 — is about 1.5%. Against the whole U.S. WWII effort, roughly 5%. The modern figures are extraordinary against single cities and single raids. They are not extraordinary against a full-scale industrial air war.

06

What the designations mean

Nearly every pairing in the DSCA notifications is a bomb body plus the kit that steers it. Read together they tell you not just what was bought, but what it was bought to do.

2,000 lb · General purpose

MK-84 & BLU-117

Functionally the same airframe. The BLU-117 is the MK-84 loaded with a thermally insensitive explosive fill rather than tritonal. DSCA notifies them interchangeably — "MK-84 or BLU-117 or a combination."

2,000 lb · Penetrator

BLU-109 & I-2000

"I-2000" (Improved 2000-lb) is the warhead family designation; BLU-109 is its principal in-service member. Notified as separate line items, identical in tactical role: bunkers and subterranean facilities.

1,000 lb

MK-83 & BLU-110A/B

The mid-weight class. BLU-110 is again the insensitive-fill variant of the MK-83 — exactly parallel to the MK-84 / BLU-117 relationship one tier up.

500 lb & below

MK-82, BLU-111, GBU-39

The GBU-39 Small Diameter Bomb is 250-lb class with folding wings: four fit where one 2,000-lb bomb would, raising targets-per-sortie and preserving heavy ordnance for hardened aim points.

Guidance

JDAM · KMU-5xx

Strap-on tail and fin kits with GPS/INS guidance. The kit number tells you the warhead: KMU-556 → MK-84. KMU-557 & 558 → BLU-109. KMU-559 → MK-83. KMU-572 → MK-82.

Initiation

FMU-152A/B fuzes

Programmable impact and delay initiators fitted before loading. Fuze volume is a leading indicator of intended expenditure — one February 2025 case carried 17,475 of them.

07

Holds, releases and waivers

The policy layer running alongside the ledger: where transfers were stopped, where they were restarted, and where the review process was simply switched off.

October 2023

Stocks diverted, stockpile drawn down

Artillery shells originally routed to Ukraine are redirected to Israel. WRSA-I stocks are drawn down. Boeing accelerates delivery of up to 1,800 JDAM kits and airlifts roughly 1,000 small diameter bombs under a pre-existing 2021 commercial contract.

9 & 29 December 2023

The first two emergency waivers

Secretary Blinken invokes emergency authority twice inside three weeks, bypassing review on more than $250 million in sales — 13,981 tank cartridges, then the fuzes and charges to complete some 14,000 artillery shells.

May 2024

One shipment held

The Biden administration pauses a single shipment — 1,800 two-thousand-pound and 1,700 five-hundred-pound bombs — citing their use in densely populated parts of Gaza ahead of an anticipated Rafah operation. The 500-lb portion is released that July; the heavy portion is not.

13 August 2024

$20.3 billion, and not one heavy bomb

The largest single notification of the period: 50 F-15IA aircraft, tank rounds, mortars, AMRAAM and tactical vehicles. It contains no 2,000-lb munitions whatsoever — a fact routinely lost in coverage of the headline figure.

Late January – February 2025

The hold is lifted

The incoming administration releases the 1,800 MK-84s; the shipment arrives in Israel on 15–16 February. Days earlier, $7.4 billion in munitions and Hellfire missiles is notified over objections from the ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

28 February 2025

Three cases, one waiver, 35,529 bombs

The largest 2,000-lb class approval on record is pushed through on emergency authority alongside 1,000-lb bodies and the D9 bulldozers previously withheld. Senator Sanders files four resolutions of disapproval against $8.56 billion in offensive weaponry. All fail.

28 February 2026

Operation Epic Fury

The United States and Israel launch a joint air campaign against Iran — Epic Fury to Washington, Roaring Lion to Jerusalem. More than 1,000 sites struck in the first 24 hours. The campaign runs to 5 May.

6 March 2026

Emergency authority, one week into the war

Secretary Rubio waives review for a package of more than 20,000 bombs. Representative Meeks: "an emergency of the Trump administration's own creation." The Senate rejects the resulting disapproval resolutions 40–59 and 36–63 in April.

15 September 2026

Two numbers, one day

The Defense Department Inspector General reports Epic Fury cost $33.4 billion through 29 June — $22.3 billion of it in expended munitions — and warns of "strategic inventory shortfalls." The same day, a $2.8 billion package of 60,000 heavy warheads for Israel surfaces at informal notification.

08

The bottleneck

The 2026 supply-side constraint is new, and it changes how every figure above should be read. Approval-to-delivery lag is now gated by American industrial capacity, not merely by contract schedules.

DoD IG · September 2026

$22.3B expended

Munitions consumed in Operation Epic Fury through 29 June 2026, out of a $33.4 billion total campaign cost. The Inspector General notes the figures were not audited.

Named constraints

Three chokepoints

Solid rocket motor production, availability of high-grade explosives and propellants, and recruitment of skilled manufacturing labour — the IG's own list.

Single point of failure

Garland, Texas

MK-80 series bomb-body production is concentrated at one facility — Repkon USA, the former General Dynamics plant acquired in March 2025 — which is also prime contractor on the March 2026 emergency case.

Requested

north of $200B

What the War Department is seeking from Congress, with stockpile replenishment identified as the hardest component to deliver.

09

Errata

Seven substantive errors were found in the source document during this revision and are recorded here rather than silently overwritten. Struck text is what the prior version claimed; the right-hand column is what the primary record shows.

Claimed

August 2024 · $20.3B package included 35,500+ MK-84 bombs.

Record

That package contained no 2,000-lb bombs at all — F-15s, tank rounds, mortars, AMRAAM, vehicles. The 35,529 figure belongs to the 28 February 2025 $2.04B case, which the prior version omitted entirely.

Claimed

January 2025 · 1,800 MK-84 and ~1,700 BLU-109 penetrators released.

Record

The 1,700 were 500-lb bombs, not penetrators — and they had already been released in July 2024. Only the 2,000-lb portion remained held into 2025.

Claimed

February 2025 · ~$6.67 billion.

Record

The February 2025 munitions case was $6.75 billion (Transmittal 24-13, 7 Feb). $6.67 billion is the January 2026 Apache-and-vehicles figure — the two appear to have been conflated.

Claimed

June 2025 · ~$647M for 3,475 KMU-557 kits for the BLU-109.

Record

$510 million (Transmittal 25-59), covering 3,845 KMU-558B/B and 3,280 KMU-572F/B. The 3,475 KMU-557 kits were in the 7 February case.

Claimed

November 2023 · ~$680M for thousands of KMU-556 JDAM and SPICE-2000 kits.

Record

31 October 2023, ~$320 million — a Rafael-to-Rafael-USA direct commercial sale of SPICE gliding bomb assemblies. No KMU-556 kits, and roughly half the stated value.

Claimed

2022 – early 2023 · ~$500–700M pre-war replenishment, ~2,500–3,500 MK-84.

Record

No public source supports this line or these quantities. Replaced with what is documented: the May 2021 Boeing commercial contract, the February 2023 $403M approval, and the $3.8B annual MOU baseline.

Claimed

Oct 2023 – Jun 2024 · ~$2.4B via Presidential Drawdown Authority, 3,000+ KMU-556 kits.

Record

The ≥14,000 MK-84 figure is sound, but the PDA attribution is not supported — the mechanisms were existing FMS/DCS cases, U.S. stocks, WRSA-I and two emergency cases. The kit figure was up to 1,800 accelerated JDAM kits.

On the figures. Congressional notifications are approvals to sell. Quantities in this ledger are what was notified, not what was delivered, except where a row is explicitly marked as transferred. Where reporting and primary notifications diverge, the notification governs. Values are estimated totals at notification and frequently differ from final contract value.

On what cannot be known. No shipment-by-shipment accounting of expended munitions exists publicly. Neither the Defense Department nor the IDF releases batch-level expenditure data. Once warheads enter Israeli depots they are fungible with existing reserves and domestic production, and no analyst can trace a given detonation to a given case.
